title: EIP-8455: RESERVOIR Opcode
description: Adds an EVM opcode that exposes the remaining state gas unavailable through GAS.
author: Javad Rajabzadeh (@ja7ad)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP introduces a new opcode, `RESERVOIR` (`0x4d`), that pushes the state gas available to the executing frame which is not included in the value returned by `GAS`. For transactions that use the reservoir model of [EIP-8037](./eip-8037.md) this is the frame's `state_gas_reservoir`. Inside an [EIP-8141](./eip-8141.md) frame transaction it is the frame's `state_gas_left`. Together with `GAS`, the opcode lets contracts read their full remaining budget and measure the gas consumed by a code region or a call, including state-gas consumption that GAS does not report. ## Motivation EIP-8037 splits the gas of a transaction into `gas_left` and a `state_gas_reservoir` that holds the part of `tx.gas` above `TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT`. State creation draws from the reservoir first and spills into `gas_left` once the reservoir is empty. The reservoir is passed in full to every child frame, and the `GAS` opcode reports `gas_left` only. Contracts therefore cannot observe their remaining state-gas budget or measure the state gas consumed by a callee. Protocols that meter sub-calls by subtracting two `gasleft()` readings, such as the [ERC-4337](./eip-4337.md) `EntryPoint`, under-count state gas whenever the reservoir pays for it: a call that creates one storage slot appears 97,920 gas cheaper when the reservoir funds the slot than when `gas_left` does. EIP-8037 points out this limitation and asks such protocols to account for state gas explicitly, but no instruction exposes the quantity they would need. The same gap affects callers of untrusted code. The `gas` argument of `CALL` bounds only execution gas, so a callee can spend the caller's entire remaining reservoir while `gasleft()` barely moves. Without visibility into the reservoir, the caller cannot notice. EIP-8141 exposes a comparable value through `TXPARAM(TXPARAM_STATE_GAS_LEFT)`, but its introspection instructions are defined only inside frame transactions and halt elsewhere. Both transaction models will be in use at the same time, and library code rarely knows which one it runs under. A single instruction that returns the state budget in either model lets such code be written once. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). ### Parameters | Constant | Value | | --- | --- | | `RESERVOIR_OPCODE` | `0x4d` | | `RESERVOIR_GAS_COST` | `2` | ### Behavior A new instruction `RESERVOIR` is introduced at `RESERVOIR_OPCODE`. It takes no stack input and pushes one value, `state_budget`, defined below. Execution of `RESERVOIR` MUST: 1. charge `RESERVOIR_GAS_COST` as execution gas to the `gas_left` of the current call frame, as `GAS` does, and halt exceptionally with out-of-gas if `gas_left` is less than `RESERVOIR_GAS_COST`. The charge MUST NOT be drawn from any state gas pool and MUST NOT change any state gas counter; 2. halt exceptionally with a stack overflow if the stack already holds 1024 items; 3. push `state_budget` as an unsigned 256-bit integer. `RESERVOIR` has no other effect. It MUST be executable in a static context. It MUST NOT be enabled in a fork in which EIP-8037 is not active. ### Definition of `state_budget` `state_budget` is the state gas available to the executing call frame that is not included in the value returned by `GAS`: | Execution context | `state_budget` | | --- | --- | | Transaction using the EIP-8037 reservoir model | `state_gas_reservoir` of the executing call frame | | EIP-8141 frame transaction | `state_gas_left` of the currently executing frame, the value `TXPARAM` returns for `TXPARAM_STATE_GAS_LEFT` | | System call | `state_gas_reservoir` that EIP-8037 places in the system call's budget | This EIP changes no accounting rule of EIP-8037 or EIP-8141. The values below follow from those rules and are listed to help implementers. ### Values under the reservoir model Let `G0` and `R0` be the values computed when EIP-8037 initializes the transaction's gas: ```python evm_gas = tx.gas - intrinsic_gas G0 = min(TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT - intrinsic_gas, evm_gas) # gas_left R0 = evm_gas - G0 # max(0, tx.gas - TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT) ``` Let `P` be the state gas charged in the pre-execution phase of [EIP-2780](./eip-2780.md): `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT × CPSB` (cost per state byte) for the deployment address of a contract-creation transaction, and the `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT × CPSB` and `STATE_BYTES_PER_AUTH_BASE × CPSB` charges applied to [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) authorizations. Since state charges draw from the reservoir first, `RESERVOIR` returns the values below, none of which exceeds `TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT`: | Situation | `RESERVOIR` returns | | --- | --- | | First instruction of the top-level frame | `max(0, R0 - P)`. At that point `gas_left` is `G0 - max(0, P - R0)` | | First instruction of a frame entered by `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE` or `CREATE2` | The caller's whole reservoir at the time of the call, after any account creation charge made by the call. The 63/64 rule does not apply to it | | Caller, after a child frame succeeds | The child's final reservoir, after the merge step of EIP-8037 | | Caller, after a child frame reverts or halts exceptionally | The reservoir restored by the rollback rules of EIP-8037 | | Caller, after a call that fails before the child frame starts | Unchanged | | After a state charge | Reduced by the part of the charge the reservoir covered, and zero if the charge exceeded it | | After a state gas refill | Increased by the part of the refill not credited to `gas_left` | ### Values inside frame transactions Inside a frame transaction, `RESERVOIR` returns the `state_gas_left` of the currently executing frame.
